senses.definition: (dated) One who has been perverted; one who has turned to error, or adopted a twisted sense of values or morals.

quotes.text: And yet it is not only tolerated, but perverts are making to it in England and this country, — perverts among the intelligent and the learned. For these things, which I have quoted, are not accusations made in a corner, but have been published in the face of the world by one of the profoundest theologians of the day, and challenge confutation.

[…] a religious pervert is ever a doubtful product. One separated from the fellows of his youth and the faith of his fathers, by acceptance of a different religion, is of necessity more or less adrift on the sea of life […]
According to the Holy Qur'an, those who cast off God's signs and follow Satan and their caprice are perverts; they are likened to dogs […]
quotes.reference: 2001, Ismāʻīl Salāmī, Islamic Views on Human Rights: Viewpoints of Iranian Scholars, page 128:

senses.definition: A person whose sexual habits are not considered acceptable.
examples: Those perverts were trying to spy on us while we changed clothes!

quotes.text: I know more damn perverts, at schools and all, than anybody you ever met, and they're always being perverty when I'm around.
quotes.reference: 1951 July 16, J[erome] D[avid] Salinger, chapter 24, in The Catcher in the Rye, Boston, Mass.: Little, Brown and Company, →OCLC:

senses.definition: (transitive) To turn another way; to divert.

quotes.text: Let's follow him, and pervert the present wrath.

senses.definition: (transitive) To corrupt; to cause to be untrue; corrupted or otherwise impure
examples: How could stopping someone from killing himself or herself "pervert the course of justice"?

quotes.text: He, in the serpent, had perverted Eve.
He was a good Proteſtant, but when he fell into the Jeſuits hands, they ſoon perverted him, and made him embrace the Roman Catholick Religion […]
quotes.reference: 1690, “The Preface to the Reader”, in A Full and True Relation of the Great and Wonderful Revolution That Hapned Lately in the Kingdom of Siam in the East-Indies, London: Randal Taylor, page vi:

quotes.text: A spokesman for Lothian and Borders Police said: "We can confirm that a 15-year-old boy has been arrested and charged in connection with the murder of Jodi Jones. A 45-year-old has also been arrested in connection with allegations of attempting to pervert the course of justice. A report on this has been sent to the procurator fiscal."
quotes.reference: 2004 April 15, “Morning swoop in hunt for Jodi's killer”, in The Scotsman:

senses.definition: To misapply, misuse, use for a nefarious purpose
examples: He has perverted his talents to dishonest gain.

senses.definition: (intransitive) To become perverted; to take the wrong course.

quotes.text: After that worde, "better is it to dey than lyve false," and al wolde perverted people false reporte make
quotes.reference: c. 1384, Thomas Usk, The Testament of Love:
